useWhen: User asks about data protection, PII, or how data is secured
Need to understand what data the system collects and where it goes
Assessing data protection compliance (GDPR, CCPA, etc.)
Building a data inventory or data flow mapping
Evaluating access controls and retention policies

workflow.description: Pull data context from Architecture Design. Identify all data stores including third-party services (payment, auth, analytics, AI APIs)
Catalog every data type with sensitivity level, location, collection method, and legal basis. Include all stores: database, file storage, cache, third-party services, logs, backups
Trace data through the system with sensitivity classification at every hop. Mark trust boundaries where data crosses between systems
Map PII through its complete lifecycle: collection, processing, storage, sharing. Assign exposure ratings (Low/Medium/High)
Build access control matrix showing who/what has access to each data type. Identify gaps and violations
Document retention periods per data type. Assess right-to-erasure support across all data stores
Synthesize findings into prioritized, specific recommendations with effort estimates and current state

examples.input: Assess data protection for a SaaS invoicing app using Stripe, PostHog, and OpenAI
examples.output: Complete data inventory with 12+ data stores identified, PII exposure analysis for customer data, access control matrix, and prioritized protection recommendations
examples.context: SaaS product with multiple third-party integrations needing GDPR compliance assessment

examples.input: What data does our product collect and how is it protected?
examples.output: Data inventory table, data flow diagrams with classification, PII lifecycle map, and protection posture rating (Strong/Adequate/Weak)
examples.context: Initial data protection assessment for a new product
